#43 Speed up TinyGL's vertex and triangle setup on the S3 [open]
TinyGL on the S3 spends about 6 us per vertex on setup, which is why GL hacks
run at 4 to 9 fps. Find out why and cut it. Measured on the spike branch
`worktree-spike-tinygl` (see `docs/tinygl-spike.md` there); depends on #42.

## Measurements

Gears with a fixed seed (a planetary set with a big ring), 466 by 466,
single-precision TinyGL, one light, a frame is 17,706 vertices and 17,620
triangles:

| Part of the frame | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Clear (colour and z, both in PSRAM) | 24.6 ms |
| Fill (a quarter-size viewport saved 30 to 35 ms) | about 40 ms |
| Vertex and triangle setup | about 100 to 120 ms |
| Push to the display (existing) | 32 ms |

Light Gears layouts (about 4,300 vertices) run at about 9 fps. Pipes probe
numbers: 3.7 ms for a 544-vertex lit sphere, about 4 us per vertex before
lighting and about 2.8 us more with it.

## Tried, and made no difference

- `-O2` instead of `-Os` for the TinyGL files (about 1 percent). Building the
  whole firmware at `-O2` crashes the compiler in `braid_single.c`.
- Specular lookup tables (`TGL_FEATURE_SPECULAR_BUFFERS`) instead of `pow`
  (needs a one-line prototype fix in `zgl.h`): no change.
- Wireframe mode: no change, because the wire sphere sends twice the vertices.

## Ideas, none tried

- Float divides are software on the S3's FPU. TinyGL's triangle setup divides
  several times per triangle. Replace with a reciprocal and multiplies, or
  fixed point. Profile first (a temporary early return in `gl_draw_triangle`,
  as the repo does for Braid).
- Put the hot vertex and triangle functions in IRAM, if flash cache misses
  turn out to matter.
- Use the second core (core 0 is mostly idle) for part of the pipeline.
- Cheaper clear: 24.6 ms for 868 KB is PSRAM write speed. A smaller or
  narrower z-buffer, or clearing only the dirty rows, might help.
- Prefer lighter Gears layouts through a `HackEntry` override, as Galaxy does
  with `count: -3`. Trades variety for speed.
- Render at a reduced size and let the push scale (changes what the push
  does, so needs a discussion).

## How to measure

`glshim.c` on the spike branch logs `GL frames= verts/frame= tris/frame=
clear= gl=` every 5 seconds. `-DGL_SPIKE_SEED=7` makes the scene repeatable
(try seeds 5 for one gear, 7 for the heavy planetary set).


--- comment:
Notes from landing Gears (PR #47). Posted by Claude, an agent working under Rod's direction.

## What landed, so you know the starting point

- TinyGL is patched at build time by `tools/tinygl_patch.py`; the GL layer is `firmware/src/glshim/`. The gotchas are in `.claude/rules/gl.md`.
- The spike's `GL frames=` log line and `-DGL_SPIKE_SEED` did not come across to main. Measure with the `run Gears fps= step= push=` line instead, or bring the spike logging back.
- Gears on the device, 48 restarts with random layouts: 2.8 to 10.0 fps, step 65 to 330 ms, push about 34 ms, wait 0. The first layout after each boot is always the same (`random()` is seeded the same way), so reboots do not sample layouts.

## Things to know before optimising

- **Specular is off by default.** TinyGL sets `zEnableSpecular = 0` unless the application calls `glSetEnableSpecular(1)`, so Gears has no highlights today and `glMateriali` has no visible effect. Turning it on is a fidelity-versus-speed decision that belongs in this issue. The shim test for `glMateriali` calls `glSetEnableSpecular(1)` for this reason.
- **Software `double` is still in the lighting and clip path.** After the single-precision patch, `gl_clipcode` and `gl_shade_vertex` still call `double` helpers: `CLIP_EPSILON` is an exponent literal, which `tools/float_literals.py` leaves alone. That is a likely contributor to the 6 us per vertex, and it is cheap to try first.
- **Every frame is a full-canvas push.** Gears dirties all 466 rows (`rows=466`), so push cost is fixed at about 32 to 34 ms regardless of layout. Anything that lets the push send fewer rows would need the dirty rectangle to be tighter than the whole canvas.
- **Clear is 24.6 ms of the frame.** TinyGL clears colour and z every frame. The z-buffer is 434 KB in PSRAM.
- **Host timing does not predict the board.** Gears costs a lot on the host too: it adds about 14 s to `test_push_present` (3,000 full pushes). Do not use the host probe to rank GL changes.

## Smaller leads

- The vertex-array shim expands `glDrawArrays` into immediate `glVertex3f` calls (`glshim.c`). Display lists recorded this way carry the expanded vertices, so any change to how lists store geometry will touch it.
- Gears' light layouts have about 4,300 vertices and its heavy ones about 17,700, so any speed-up shows most on the heavy layouts. `*cycles` and `*ncolors` are overridden to 0 and 64 in `registry.c`.
- Upstream `free_gears` leaks `bp->gears` (36 to 1,620 B of internal heap per start; about 14 KB over 48 restarts). Not a speed issue, but it will show up in any long restart test.


--- comment:
Status update from Claude (an agent working under Rod's direction), as of the end of the 2026-10-09/10 session. Everything below is on `main`.

## What landed

- **#51, clip epsilon.** `CLIP_EPSILON` was `1E-5`, a double, so `gl_clipcode` ran a software double multiply on every vertex. It is now `1E-5f`. On the board, CubicGrid's step (8,000 unlit points, a deterministic boot) fell by a flat 5.6 ms in every window (about 11 percent, 0.7 us a vertex); Morph3D by about 3 ms. Frame hashes are unchanged.
- **#52, dirty rectangle.** TinyGL reports the box around everything it draws. `glClear` clears only the box drawn since the last clear and a swap marks only what was drawn and what the clear erased, so the push sends those rows. A new context and a new clear colour are full clears. Morph3D's step fell from 75 to 83 ms to 55 to 59 and its push from 32.5 ms to 2 to 9 (91 to 192 rows of 466); Gears' first layout step from 65 to 79 ms to 44 to 63 and push from 32 to 34 to 4 to 12. CubicGrid pays about 1 ms for the bookkeeping and gains nothing, as its points cover the whole screen.
- **The hacks' own pauses.** The work shrank, but the frame rate barely moved, because each hack asks for a pause after every frame and the loop credits only the push against it. Morph3D (40 ms) and Gears (30 ms) now register `*delay: 10000`. Result: Morph3D 8.4 fps at the start of the evening to 14.4 to 15.2; Gears' first layout 9.0 to 10.2 to 12.6 to 17.6 (about 14.5 on average). A heavy Gears layout is render-bound and gains little.

Tests: pinned frame hashes are unchanged for every hack, so output is pixel-identical, and the shadow-display replay passes. The review on #52 found five issues (one real bug: right-to-left lines left stale pixels); all are fixed and tested.

## Where a frame goes (CubicGrid, 8,000 points, 46.7 ms step)

Measured with temporary early returns in TinyGL, never committed. Colour clear 12.7 ms (27 percent, about 34 MB/s, so memory bandwidth); vertex pipeline 13.3 ms (28 percent, about 1.7 us a vertex); drawing the points 11.1 ms (24 percent, about 1.4 us a point); list read and dispatch about 9.6 ms (21 percent; the cause is my guess, probably PSRAM reads). Details and the dirty-rectangle numbers are in `docs/gl-budget.md`.

## Checked and ruled out

- **Software `double` in lighting.** After #51 the only soft-double references left in TinyGL are per call (`glFrustum`, `glopLight`, `glopRotate`, `glClearDepth`, a debug printer), plus two `1E-3` compares in `gl_shade_vertex` that run only for positional lights and specular. Gears and Morph3D use directional lights with specular off, so they never run; I did not patch them without a hack to time.
- **Skipping the z clear.** CubicGrid clears colour only, and Gears and Morph3D need depth.
- **Host timing** still does not predict the board; the harness (`tools/gl_budget.py`) counts work and predicted frame times to about 10 percent before the dirty rectangle, but its clear and push constants now overstate sparse hacks and need a refit.

## Ideas from the first list, and where they stand

- Float divides in triangle setup: not measured.
- IRAM for the hot functions, and using core 0: not tried.
- Cheaper clear: done for sparse scenes by the dirty rectangle.
- Lighter Gears layouts through an override: not done (the pause change helped the light ones; the heavy ones are still 3 to 5 fps).
- Render at a reduced size: not done.
- **New:** overlap the push with the next frame (core 0 pushes, core 1 renders), which could take a frame from step plus push to the larger of the two. It needs a second 434 KB buffer and a lock around M5GFX, and PSRAM bandwidth may limit the gain. Untried.

## Open decisions and gaps

- Specular is still off (fidelity versus speed); not decided.
- Only Gears' first layout after boot was timed with the dirty rectangle, not the heavy layouts; nobody has run the new build for long.
- Morph3D's two middle shapes have never appeared on the board, and CubicGrid has had no long run: #50.

Correction to my status comment above, from Claude (an agent working under Rod's direction).

I wrote that the harness (`tools/gl_budget.py`) "counts work and predicted frame times to about 10 percent before the dirty rectangle". That holds for Gears and CubicGrid but **not for Morph3D**, which the model under-predicted by 11 to 20 percent.

What went wrong: I had matched Morph3D's earlier measured steps to its shapes by size alone, and matched them to the wrong ones. Morph3D has five shapes (2,300, 3,864, 5,040, 5,100 and 7,200 vertices), not four. An overnight capture on the final code (2h13m, 795 rotations, no resets) showed four step clusters (about 21, 40, 55 and 74 ms), and the earlier 48 ms and 78 to 82 ms steps were the 2,300 and the 5,040 or 5,100 vertex shapes. The cause of the error is the first worry from the review: Morph3D has two lights and the model charged one lighting cost per lit vertex.

The fix is in #53: the harness now counts a light term for each enabled light, which reproduces all five shapes (predicted old steps of 48, 66, 80 or 82 and 102 ms against 48 and 78 to 82 measured directly and about 45, 65, 81 and 102 inferred). The same capture found no PSRAM leak, and attributes the internal heap drift (about 388 bytes a lap) to Gears' known upstream leak rather than to Morph3D or CubicGrid.

Nothing in the optimisation numbers above changes; this is about the harness's accuracy, not the speed-ups. Until #53 merges, `docs/gl-budget.md` on `main` still has the wrong Morph3D rows.


#44 Pipes on TinyGL: too slow as written, and what would change that [open]
Pipes was the first GL hack tried and it is not viable on TinyGL as written.
Record what was learned and what would change that. Depends on #42; see also
#43. Data is in `docs/tinygl-spike.md` on branch `worktree-spike-tinygl`.

## Why it is slow

Pipes does not accumulate. Every frame it clears and redraws every piece so
far from display lists (`draw_pipes` loops over `system_index`), up to about
500 pieces per system with the defaults, under a slowly rotating camera. Cost
grows with the pipe, and every frame changes completely, so pushing only the
changed rows saves nothing.

With Pipes' real primitives (triangle-strip spheres of 16 by 16, 24-facet
quad-strip tubes), measured on the S3 at 464 by 464:

- 3.7 ms per piece, plus about 80 ms fixed per frame.
- 2.8 fps at 80 pieces, 1.2 fps at 210, under 1 fps by 250.
- Wireframe (`*wireframe: True`) is no faster: the same frame times, because
  the cost is per vertex and the wire sphere sends twice the vertices.
- 8 by 8 spheres (about 3.7 times fewer triangles) gave 5.2 fps at 50 pieces,
  3.4 at 100. Not enough on its own.

## What would change that

- Stop redrawing the settled scene. The camera turns only 0.02 degrees per
  frame, so drawing just the newest piece onto the existing frame, and
  redrawing everything only now and then, would make the cost per frame
  constant. Needs interception at the GL layer and slightly changes the look
  (the older pieces lag the camera).
- Faster vertex setup in TinyGL (#43).

## Port notes

- The real spheres come from `unit_sphere` in `sphere.c`, which builds
  `glVertexPointer` arrays and calls `glDrawArrays` inside a display list.
  TinyGL gets that wrong; the array shim from #42 fixes it.
- Pipes also needs `buildlwo.c`, `teapot.c` (built unconditionally),
  `sphere.c`, `gltrackball.c` and `rotator.c`. All are in `hacks/glx/`, so
  they can be copied byte-identical.
- Pipes uses two lights' state and a specular material.


#45 Choose the next GL hacks after Gears (survey of 146, nothing measured yet) [closed]
Which GL hacks to try after Gears (#42). This is a static survey of the
xscreensaver 6.16 sources; nothing here is measured on the device.

## What the scan looked at

All 146 GL hacks in `hacks/glx/`, flagging use of features TinyGL lacks or
handles poorly:

| Feature | Hacks using it |
| --- | --- |
| Textures | 87 |
| Blending (`GL_BLEND`, `glBlendFunc`) | 84 |
| Fog | 17 |
| Stencil | 2 |
| Pixel read-back or copy | 4 |
| Accumulation buffer | 0 |

TinyGL's blending ignores alpha, so blend-only hacks may degrade rather than
fail. Only 36 hacks are clear of all six.

## Clear of all six

`stonerview`, `sproingiewrap`, `swim`, `b_lockglue`, `dangerball`,
`moebiusgears`, `glknots`, `covid19`, `hilbert`, `bubble3d`, `sierpinski3d`,
`splodesic`, `cubicgrid`, `hexstrut`, `pipes`, `kallisti`, `cubestorm`,
`cubetwist`, `morph3d`, `superquadrics`, `surfaces`, `voronoi`, `hextrail`,
`menger`, `topblock`, `gears`, `razzledazzle`, `cityflow`, `sproingies`,
`companion`, `rubik`, `shark`, `whale`, `dolphin`, `gltext`.

Blend only (no textures, fog, stencil or read-back): `antinspect`, `beats`,
`blinkbox`, `boing`, `crackberg`, `crumbler`, `cubestack`, `deepstars`,
`geodesic`, `hydrostat`, `hypertorus`, `hypnowheel`, `kaleidocycle`,
`lockward`, `nakagin`, `polytopes`, `tronbit`, `unknownpleasures`.

## Shortlist, and why

Speed is roughly 6 us per lit vertex plus about 80 ms fixed per frame (#43),
so the question is vertices per frame, not features. Estimates only:

- `morph3d`: morphing lit polyhedra, no growth. Probably small.
- `stonerview`: 155 lines, no lighting or textures.
- `kallisti`: small and lit. Read it first.
- `gears`: done in #42.

Probably too heavy: `superquadrics` (25 objects at up to 50 by 50),
`moebiusgears` (17 gears), `glknots` (800 segments), `dangerball` (a 32-slice
sphere with spikes), `cubestorm` (snakes of 200 cubes), `menger`,
`pipes` (#44).

## Suggested next step

Measure instead of guessing. The spike already counts vertices and triangles
per frame inside TinyGL. A host harness that runs a hack against it would
give a polygon budget for each candidate without a flash. Once the GL layer
from #42 is in, that harness is a small step.

Features TinyGL lacks that other hacks will hit: `glTexGeni`, `glFog*`,
`glInterleavedArrays` (see the Flying Toasters issue).

# GL layer and TinyGL gotchas

OpenGL hacks run on TinyGL, a software OpenGL (C-Chads fork, commit
`36a7987`, zlib-style licence). Issues #42 to #46 hold the numbers and ideas.

- `src/tinygl/` is byte-identical to upstream and excluded from every env.
  `firmware/patch_tinygl.py` runs `tools/tinygl_patch.py` and writes the
  patched tree, plus one unity file, into `.pio/build/<env>/generated/`;
  `glshim/tinygl_build.c` compiles it. Each patch checks its anchor and fails
  with "has upstream changed?". TinyGL's README allows building it as one
  unit, and it compiles cleanly that way.
- A GL hack gets `USE_GL` from a one-line wrapper: `hacks/<name>_gl.c` for
  the hack, `glshim/glx_<name>.c` for each helper copied to
  `xs_support/glx/`. Exclude the copies in all three envs' `build_src_filter`
  and keep `-Isrc/xs_support/glx` in `build_flags`. Never define `HAVE_GL`:
  it adds `glx_context` to `ModeInfo`, which `xlockmore.c` (built without
  it) allocates smaller. Build each helper as its own unit: `tube.h` and
  `normals.h` define clashing types.
- TinyGL draws straight into `canvas->px` at the canvas size, with its
  pixel packer patched to the canvas's byte-swapped RGB565. Test colours
  with exact `rgb565()` values: white looks the same either way round.
- Display list name 0 means "invalid" to hacks (`if (!glGenLists(1)) abort()`)
  and TinyGL handed it out first; the patch starts at 1. Its list buffers
  are 64 slots, not 4,096: each list took 16 KB and 500 lists overflowed
  PSRAM (boot loop, `StoreProhibited` at `0x4000` in `alloc_list`).
- TinyGL counts vertex-array stride in floats and reads the array when a

# GL budget: cubicgrid and morph3d

`tools/gl_budget.py` runs a GL hack on the host, counts what each frame asks of
TinyGL, and predicts the device frame time. It was built to choose between two
candidates for the next GL port (issue #45) without flashing either.

```text
uv run tools/gl_budget.py [--frames N] [--seeds a,b,c]
    [--override '*name: value' ...] name[:seed] ...
```

Gears is read from `firmware/src/hacks/gears/`; any other name from
`vendor/xscreensaver-6.16/hacks/glx/` (git-ignored, never copied into the
repo). A hack that does not build is reported with its first error, and the
exit status is 1.

`--override` gives the hack a resource line that beats its own defaults, as an
entry in `registry.c`'s override list does on the device. Repeat it for more.
It applies to every hack named, so run hacks with different overrides
separately. Use it to try a registry override (`--override '*count: 40'`)
before committing to it, or to supply one a hack needs to start.

## What it counts

The counters sit inside a private copy of TinyGL, built only for the tool
(`firmware/src/tinygl/` and the firmware builds are untouched). Counting there
means a display list that is built once and replayed every frame is counted on
every frame. Per frame, it records:

- **Vertices** set up, and how many of them were lit.
- **Triangles** rasterised, after back-face culling, and the **pixels** they
  cover (screen area, overdraw included, capped at the canvas).
- **Lines** and **points** drawn.

## The cost model

A frame costs a fixed 56.6 ms (clear 24.6 ms, display push 32 ms), plus 4 us
per vertex, 2.8 us more for each enabled light on each lit vertex (both from the
Pipes probe in #43, measured with one light), plus a fill term. The fill term
is 570 ns a pixel, fitted so that the heavy Gears scene (seed 13, 17,700
vertices) costs the 40 ms of fill that #43 measured.

Checked against Gears, the only hack with device numbers. The fit and the
tests use 60 frames; the table below is a 300 frame run, and Gears' pixel
count drifts by about 15 percent between the two as the gears turn (at 60
frames the heavy scene is 217 ms and its fill is exactly 40 ms; at 300 it is
211 ms and 34 ms):

| Scene | Predicted | Measured (#43) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gears seed 13, heavy | 211 ms, 4.7 fps | 197 to 217 ms, about 5 fps |
| Gears seed 11, light (held out) | 117 ms, 8.5 fps | about 111 ms, 9 fps |

The light scene was not used in the fit and lands within 6 percent.

188	separately. Use it to try a registry override (`--override '*count: 40'`)
189	before committing to it, or to supply one a hack needs to start.
190	
191	## What it counts
192	
193	The counters sit inside a private copy of TinyGL, built only for the tool
194	(`firmware/src/tinygl/` and the firmware builds are untouched). Counting there
195	means a display list that is built once and replayed every frame is counted on
196	every frame. Per frame, it records:
197	
198	- **Vertices** set up, and how many of them were lit.
199	- **Triangles** rasterised, after back-face culling, and the **pixels** they
200	  cover (screen area, overdraw included, capped at the canvas).
201	- **Lines** and **points** drawn.
202	
203	## The cost model
204	
205	A frame costs a fixed 56.6 ms (clear 24.6 ms, display push 32 ms), plus 4 us
206	per vertex, 2.8 us more for each enabled light on each lit vertex (both from the
207	Pipes probe in #43, measured with one light), plus a fill term. The fill term
208	is 570 ns a pixel, fitted so that the heavy Gears scene (seed 13, 17,700
209	vertices) costs the 40 ms of fill that #43 measured.
210	
211	Checked against Gears, the only hack with device numbers. The fit and the
212	tests use 60 frames; the table below is a 300 frame run, and Gears' pixel
213	count drifts by about 15 percent between the two as the gears turn (at 60
214	frames the heavy scene is 217 ms and its fill is exactly 40 ms; at 300 it is
215	211 ms and 34 ms):
216	
217	| Scene | Predicted | Measured (#43) |
218	| --- | --- | --- |
219	| Gears seed 13, heavy | 211 ms, 4.7 fps | 197 to 217 ms, about 5 fps |
220	| Gears seed 11, light (held out) | 117 ms, 8.5 fps | about 111 ms, 9 fps |
221	
222	The light scene was not used in the fit and lands within 6 percent.
223	
224	## The comparison
225	
226	Means over 300 frames after a 10 frame warm-up. Both hacks are lit or point
227	based, so the fixed 56.6 ms sets a ceiling of about 17.7 fps for anything.
228	
229	| Hack | Vertices | Triangles | Points | Predicted | fps |
230	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
231	| morph3d, four of its five shapes (seeds 1 to 8) | 3,864 to 7,200 | 2,300 to 4,000 | 0 | 87 to 114 ms | 8.8 to 11.5 |
232	| cubicgrid, default `ticks` 30 | 27,000 | 0 | 27,000 | 165 ms | 6.1 |
233	
234	- **morph3d** is lit and vertex-bound, but treat 9 to 11 fps as optimistic.
235	  It enables two lights and two-sided lighting, and TinyGL shades once per
236	  light, while the model's lighting cost was measured with one (about +20 ms
237	  for seed 1). Its triangles are also tiny, 3 to 4 pixels each against 15 to
238	  29 in the Gears scenes the fill figure was fitted to. The fill term absorbs
239	  per-triangle cost at Gears' ratio, so it under-predicts here: if all of
240	  Gears' fill were per-triangle cost, morph3d's would be about 35 ms rather
241	  than 8. Together these could put morph3d nearer 6 to 8 fps.
242	- **cubicgrid** draws a 30 by 30 by 30 grid of points (`ticks` cubed) from a
243	  display list every frame. At the default that is 27,000 vertices, which is
244	  why it lands at about 6 fps. The model does not cost the points themselves,
245	  and they are drawn 2.5 pixels wide (`bigdots` defaults to True), so 6 fps is
246	  an optimistic floor too.
247	- Its size is a resource. Setting `*ticks` through a `HackEntry` override, as
248	  Galaxy does with `*count`, shrinks the cost with the cube, by the same

251	
252	## Verdict

254	Port **morph3d** first, but the margin is narrower than the first numbers

257	digits; cubicgrid at its default is at best 6 fps and probably worse, and needs

261	tool can be taught the two-light and small-triangle cases from it.

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: writes the patched TinyGL tree, and the one
translation unit that includes it, into the build directory. The tree in
src/tinygl/ stays byte-identical to upstream; see tools/tinygl_patch.py."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
sys.path.insert(0, str(project.parent / "tools"))
import tinygl_patch  # noqa: E402

source = project / "src" / "tinygl"
sources = {
    str(path.relative_to(source)): path.read_text(errors="surrogateescape")
    for sub in ("src", "include")
    for path in sorted((source / sub).rglob("*"))
    if path.is_file()
}
patched = tinygl_patch.patch_tree(sources)

generated = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated"  # noqa: F821


def write_if_changed(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Rewrites only a changed file, so the build does not recompile it."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = text.encode(errors="surrogateescape")
    if not path.exists() or path.read_bytes() != data:
        path.write_bytes(data)


for relative, text in patched.items():
    write_if_changed(generated / "tinygl" / relative, text)
write_if_changed(generated / "tinygl_unity.c", tinygl_patch.unity_source(patched))

# `GL/gl.h` and `zbuffer.h` resolve to the patched copy, and
# src/glshim/tinygl_build.c finds the unity file.
env.Append(  # noqa: F821
    CPPPATH=[str(generated / "tinygl" / "include"), str(generated)]
)

"""Reads the StopWatch's serial log into a file for a number of seconds.

    .venv/bin/python -I tools/serial_capture.py <out-file> <seconds> [port]

Opening the port resets the board (a random hack starts, the overlay returns to
nothing), and a flash or a crash makes the port go away and come back, so this
reopens it in a loop. Run it in the background with absolute paths; background
shells ignore `cd`. The `run <hack> fps= step= push= ...` lines are explained in
AGENTS.md ("Serial log").
"""

import sys
import time

import serial

DEFAULT_PORT = "/dev/cu.usbmodem112401"


def capture(out: str, seconds: float, port: str = DEFAULT_PORT) -> None:
    end = time.time() + seconds
    with open(out, "wb") as f:
        while time.time() < end:
            try:
                with serial.Serial(port, 115200, timeout=1) as s:
                    while time.time() < end:
                        f.write(s.read(4096))
                        f.flush()
            except (serial.SerialException, OSError):
                time.sleep(0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    capture(sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]), *(sys.argv[3:]))

"""Flash builds of the firmware in turn and compare their serial logs.

    .venv/bin/python -I tools/ab_flash.py --hack CubicGrid --seconds 60 \\
        --rounds 2 --out /tmp/ab base= iram=-DGL_IRAM "prof=-DGL_PROFILE -DGL_IRAM"

Each `name=flags` is a variant. Every variant is built once, pinned to the
hack with rotation off (`START_HACK`, `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), and its image kept.
Then, round by round, each image is flashed and the serial log captured for
`--seconds`. A boot is deterministic, so alternating builds and comparing
window by window is how this repo measures a change (AGENTS.md).

This flashes the device: run it only with Rod's go-ahead. It never touches
the partition table or `ffat`; `pio run -t upload` writes what a normal
upload writes.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
FIRMWARE = ROOT / "firmware"
IMAGE = FIRMWARE / ".pio" / "build" / "stopwatch" / "firmware.bin"

RUN = re.compile(r"^run (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
GLPROF = re.compile(r"^glprof (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
FIELD = re.compile(r"(\w+)=([-\d.]+)")


def parse_fields(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """`fps=12.3 step=45.6ms rows=466` to {"fps": 12.3, "step": 45.6, ...}."""
    return {k: float(v) for k, v in FIELD.findall(text)}


@dataclass
class Capture:
    runs: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
    glprof: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_log(text: str, hack: str) -> Capture:
    """The `run` and `glprof` windows a log has for `hack` (any case)."""
    out = Capture()
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        for pattern, bucket in ((RUN, out.runs), (GLPROF, out.glprof)):
            m = pattern.match(line)
            if m and m.group("hack").lower() == hack.lower():
                bucket.append(parse_fields(m.group("fields")))
    return out


def summarise(windows: list[dict[str, float]], skip: int = 1) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Mean of each field, leaving out the first `skip` windows: the first
    holds the boot and, for push, the name overlay (AGENTS.md)."""
    kept = windows[skip:]
    if not kept:
        return {}
    keys = sorted({k for w in kept for k in w})
    return {k: statistics.fmean(w[k] for w in kept if k in w) for k in keys}


def render(results: dict[str, list[Capture]], keys: list[str]) -> str:
    lines = [
        "| Variant | Round | Windows | " + " | ".join(keys) + " |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | " + " | ".join("---" for _ in keys) + " |",
    ]
    for name, captures in results.items():
        for i, cap in enumerate(captures, 1):
            merged = summarise(cap.runs)
            merged.update(summarise(cap.glprof))
            cells = [f"{merged[k]:.2f}" if k in merged else "-" for k in keys]
            lines.append(f"| {name} | {i} | {max(len(cap.runs) - 1, 0)} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def pio(*args: str, flags: str = "") -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR": str(ROOT / ".platformio"),
        "NO_COLOR": "1",
        "PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS": flags,
    }
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(ROOT / ".venv" / "bin" / "pio"), "run", "-d", str(FIRMWARE), "-e", "stopwatch", *args],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )


def build(name: str, flags: str, hack: str, out: Path) -> Path:
    pinned = f'-DSTART_HACK=\\"{hack}\\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=0 {flags}'.strip()
    result = pio(flags=pinned)
    (out / f"build-{name}.log").write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(f"build of {name} failed; see {out / f'build-{name}.log'}")
    image = out / f"{name}.bin"
    shutil.copyfile(IMAGE, image)
    return image


def flash(image: Path, log: Path) -> None:
    shutil.copyfile(image, IMAGE)
    result = pio("-t", "nobuild", "-t", "upload")
    log.write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    if result.returncode != 0 or "Hash of data verified" not in result.stdout:
        sys.exit(f"flash of {image.name} did not verify; see {log}")


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--hack", required=True, help="a name from g_hacks[]")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=60)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--keys", default="fps,step,push,rows")
    parser.add_argument("variants", nargs="+", help="name=flags")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
    import serial_capture

    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    variants = dict(v.split("=", 1) for v in args.variants)
    images = {name: build(name, flags, args.hack, args.out) for name, flags in variants.items()}
    results: dict[str, list[Capture]] = {name: [] for name in variants}
    for r in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        for name, image in images.items():
            flash(image, args.out / f"flash-{r}-{name}.log")
            log = args.out / f"serial-{r}-{name}.log"
            serial_capture.capture(str(log), args.seconds)
            results[name].append(parse_log(log.read_text(errors="replace"), args.hack))
    table = render(results, args.keys.split(","))
    (args.out / "summary.md").write_text(table)
    print(table, end="")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
